First of all, I'm genuinely curious to hear general information from anyone who practices a vegan ketogenic diet, either periodically or primarily. So if that's you, please do share some of your knowledge and experience.

Alright, so please bear with me while I give a rather long-winded and rambling explanation of why I am posting this. Normally, I follow a high carbohydrate, low fat, low salt, low oil vegan diet. It's worked well for me, which is saying a lot for any diet because I am very lazy when it comes to food preparation. If I can't microwave it or just eat it straight away, then I don't buy it. Anyway, two nights ago, I bought a small plastic jar of peanut butter. I needed the jar to use for storage in one of the bottle cages of my touring bike. Peanut butter is obviously a very high fat food. The next morning, I started the process of eating the peanut butter in order to empty the jar so I can use it.

Since I was suddenly introducing a huge amount of fat to my diet, I decided to drastically reduce my amount of carbs to compensate1. For my meals, I simply added peanut butter to chopped broccoli, cauliflower, and mushrooms mixed with shiritaki noodles and then I simply microwaved it. Surprisingly, it doesn't taste half bad (to me). For breakfast, I also had 2 apples in addition to this. In this way, I got through the majority of the jar. Today I will be finishing the rest of the jar in the same way.

There are a few things I noticed. The first is that I feel like shit. As I said, I normally follow a high carb low fat diet. Going abruptly to high fat low carb had me feeling awful by about noon on the first day, and I still feel awful after breakfast. In fact, I feel even worse today than I did yesterday. The second thing I noticed is that I am a bit sluggish mentally, which makes sense because the brain primarily runs on carbs like any other muscle. Another thing I noticed was that I wasn't as hungry as I normally am. The peanut butter may have been responsible for suppressing my appetite (although I should note here that I was noticeably hungrier at night). The last major thing I noticed is that within 24 hours of starting this temporary switch, I've lost 4 pounds.

I weigh myself every morning after I poop, and my bowels are quite reliable and regular thanks to my high fiber intake. I understand that a daily fluctuation in weight of a few pounds can be normal, but my weight normally only fluctuates by a single pound from day to day. So, where did those 4 entire pounds come from? Water? My water intake didn't change. Fat? I don't think it's possible to burn that much fat in 24 hours. Glycogen? The same may apply. Burning 4 pounds of glycogen in 24 hours may not be possible, especially since I didn't exercise yesterday.

So what happened?

1 The reason for carb reduction when increasing fat intake is to decrease fat storage. Ideally, fat should be kept low while carbs should be kept high, because this is the optimal way for the body to function while keeping fat storage to a minimum. The human body burns carbs preferentially, while it stores consumed fat very efficiently and directly as body fat. The thinking is that one should either keep carbs or fat low, but never combine the two in sufficient amounts to cause weight gain.
